newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan cereals crop seen at up to 8.0 mln T in 9.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan cereals crop seen at up to 8.0 mln T in 9.

text.p: Morocco will produce 7.0 to 8.0 million tonnes of cereals in 1996/97 season, due to plenty of rains this winter, according to a Moroccan think-tank, the Centre Marocain de Conjoncture (CMC).

"Despite the delay registered in the sowing operations, we forecast a good cereal harvest of between 7.0 and 8.0 million tonnnes this year," Abdelali Doumou, an analyst at Casablanca-based CMC, told Reuters on Friday.
Morocco harvested a record 10 million tonnes of cereals last year after a severe drought in 1995, the Statistics Directorate said in a recent revised report.

Doumou, commenting on a recent survey by the centre, said: "More than 65 percent of arable lands have been sown so far...We expect the remaining surface to be sowed by maize and sunflower crops in spring, starting from March."
Heavy rains in December were behind the delay in ploughing lands at the normal time, the centre said.

Floods have hit nearly 20,000 hectares of cereals and sugar crops, mainly in the Ghrab and Loukkos regions, officials said. The rich farming Gharb and Loukkos areas are located in the north of Morocco.
But the CMC analyst said the floods would have no impact on agricultural output.
According to the national meteorological centre, some agricultural areas received more than double the amount of rains in December compared with the same period in 1995.
The outlook for the harvest will also depend on the weather in the coming weeks, CMC said in a newsletter.
"If ploughing speeds up in the first quarter of 1997, Moroccan agriculture will register 70 percent performance compared with the 1995/96 season," it said.

According to the agriculture ministry, a total of 5.6 million hectares are expected to be sown for all crops in the 1996/97 season, similar to the area for 1995/96. Nearly 900,000 hectares are located in irrigated areas, it added. - Ali Bouzerda, Rabat newsroom +212-7 726518
